Subject: Light Up a Life — draft for Moira to review before posting

Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the bookshop window again this year. Hilary asked here the other day whether we were doing it, as her mum’s name was on it last year and she would like to bring her sister this time. Yes, Hilary, we are, and we shall be very glad to see you both.

It is seven years this month since my husband, Ray, died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag on the tree, I could hardly write it. Now I write it at the shop counter, with the same pen. It is still his name, and I still have to stop for a moment, but I am glad to have somewhere to put it.

I know I am not the only person who finds that a small thing like this can matter rather a lot. Last year there were 412 tags on our tree. Thank you to everyone who wrote one, brought someone along, or simply stopped by the window. Thank you, too, to those who helped hang the tags and made room for people to take their time. You helped make it a place where nobody had to explain why they were feeling a little quiet.

Memory tags will be available in the shop from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. There will be envelopes on the counter if you would rather take yours home and write it there. Some people know exactly what they want to write; others need a bit of time over it. Either is quite all right.

We shall switch the lights on at 4pm on Saturday 28 November. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing a few carols, and Doreen is making mince pies again. Judging by last year, I wouldn’t leave it too late for those.

Every name on the tags will be read aloud at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December, at 3pm in the day centre. You do not have to attend the service for your loved one’s name to be read.

And please remember that the tree is for anyone who is grieving, not only for families who have been cared for by the hospice. Whether your loss is recent or many years ago, you are welcome.

You are also very welcome just to come and stand by the tree. You needn’t buy a book, write a tag, or find anything to say. If you would like a little company, we are there. If you would rather have a quiet moment, that is fine too.

Jean
